name: Media & Entertainment
tagline: Views, watch time, unique viewers, completion, subscribers and revenue for streaming, video and publishing, plus catalogues and box office
description: Viewing and listening logs (Netflix viewing activity, Spotify streaming history, OTT play logs from Hotstar, JioCinema, ZEE5 or SonyLIV), content performance exports from YouTube Studio, Spotify for Artists, Chartbeat, Parse.ly and publisher dashboards, content catalogues (Netflix titles, Spotify tracks, IMDb and TMDB extracts) and box-office trackers (Box Office Mojo, The Numbers, Indian day-wise collections).

fields.label: Title
fields.description: The title, track, video, article or film each row is about.

fields.label: Audio feature
fields.description: One of the audio features Spotify reports per track.

subDomains.name: Viewing and listening activity
subDomains.description: One row per play, view or stream (or per title per day) with the viewer, the title, when it was watched and for how long, as in Netflix viewing activity, Spotify streaming history and OTT play logs.

subDomains.name: Content performance
subDomains.description: One row per video, article, episode or track (often per day) with views, watch time, likes, comments, shares, subscribers gained and revenue, as in YouTube Studio, Spotify for Artists, Chartbeat or Parse.ly exports.

subDomains.name: Content catalogue
subDomains.description: One row per title, track or video in a library with type, genre, release year or date, runtime, rating and popularity, as in the Netflix titles dataset, Spotify track lists and IMDb or TMDB extracts.

subDomains.name: Box office
subDomains.description: One row per film (or per film per weekend or territory) with release date, distributor, opening and total gross, budget, screens and verdict, as in Box Office Mojo, The Numbers or Indian box-office trackers.

kpis.name: Views
kpis.definition: Views, plays or streams in the period.
kpis.formula: Sum of the views column, or one per row of a viewing log

variants.label: Rows (one per view or play)
variants.caveat: No views column, so each row is counted as one view or play.

pitfalls: Each platform counts a view its own way (a YouTube view, a Netflix two-minute view, a Spotify 30-second stream), so compare views within one platform.

kpis.name: Watch time (hours)
kpis.definition: Total time spent watching or listening, in hours.
kpis.formula: Sum of watch time, converted to hours

kpis.name: Unique viewers
kpis.definition: Distinct people who watched, listened or read in the period.

variants.label: Unique viewers column (summed)
variants.caveat: Summed across rows, so someone who watched several titles or on several days counts more than once.

pitfalls: Recounted for every period and group; viewers of two titles never add up to the total.

kpis.name: Average view duration (minutes)
kpis.definition: Average minutes watched or listened per view or play.
pitfalls: Longer titles naturally get longer views; compare like with like (shorts with shorts, films with films).

kpis.name: Watch time per viewer (hours)
kpis.definition: Average hours each viewer or listener spent in the period.

kpis.name: Completion rate
kpis.definition: Share of views or plays watched or listened to the end.
pitfalls: Platforms mark a view complete at different points (end credits, 90% watched), so compare within one platform.

kpis.name: Net subscribers
kpis.definition: Subscribers or followers gained minus those lost in the period.

variants.label: Subscribers gained
variants.caveat: No subscribers-lost column, so this counts gains only.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.definition: Revenue earned from the content in the period: ads, subscriptions shares or royalties.
pitfalls: Platform revenue figures are estimates that are revised after the month closes.

kpis.name: Titles
kpis.definition: Titles, tracks, videos or films in the table; with a date range, those added or released in it.

variants.label: Distinct titles
variants.caveat: No content ID, so titles with the same name (remakes, covers) count once.

variants.label: Row count
variants.caveat: No title or ID column, so every row is counted as one title. Check the grain.

kpis.name: Average rating
kpis.definition: Average audience or critic rating across rated titles.
pitfalls: A title rated by a handful of people counts as much as one rated by millions; read it next to the vote count.

kpis.name: Average runtime (minutes)
kpis.definition: Average length of a title, track or video, in minutes.

kpis.name: Movies % of titles
kpis.definition: Share of titles that are movies rather than series or episodes.

kpis.name: Average popularity
kpis.definition: Average popularity score the platform gives its titles or tracks.
pitfalls: Popularity scores are relative and recalculated by the platform, so they compare titles at one moment, not over time.

kpis.name: Box office gross
kpis.definition: Ticket sales of the films released in the period.

variants.label: Domestic gross
variants.caveat: No worldwide gross column, so this is the domestic market only.

pitfalls: Grosses are in nominal money of their year; old films look smaller than they were.

kpis.name: Average gross per film
kpis.definition: Box office gross divided across the films released.
pitfalls: A few blockbusters dominate box office, so the average sits far above the typical film; read the top films too.

kpis.name: Gross-to-budget multiple
kpis.definition: How many times their production budgets the films grossed, over films with both figures.
kpis.formula: Gross ÷ production budget, over films with both

variants.label: Domestic gross ÷ budget
variants.caveat: No worldwide gross column, so only the domestic market is set against the budget.

pitfalls: Studios keep only part of the gross (exhibitors take a share) and spend on marketing too, so a film usually needs well above 1× its budget to break even.

kpis.name: Opening share of gross
kpis.definition: Share of the total gross earned on the opening day or weekend: how front-loaded the run was.
kpis.formula: Opening gross ÷ total gross, over films with both

variants.label: Opening ÷ gross
variants.caveat: Opening figures are often for the home market while the total may be worldwide; check both cover the same market.

kpis.name: Hit rate
kpis.definition: Share of films with a verdict that were hits (hit, super hit or blockbuster).

variants.label: Hit verdicts ÷ films with a verdict

pitfalls: Verdicts come from trade sources with their own rules; which grades count as hits is set in Check & map › Value meanings.

kpis.name: Titles watched
kpis.definition: Distinct titles, tracks or videos that were watched or listened to in the period.
kpis.formula: Count of distinct titles with activity

kpis.name: Views per viewer
kpis.definition: Average views or plays per unique viewer.

kpis.name: Skip rate
kpis.definition: Share of plays the listener skipped before the end.

kpis.name: Views per title
kpis.definition: Average views or plays per title that had activity.
pitfalls: Views are concentrated in a few hits, so the average sits well above the typical title.

kpis.name: Engagement rate
kpis.definition: Likes, comments and shares per view.

variants.label: (Likes + comments) ÷ views
variants.caveat: No shares column, so only likes and comments are counted.

pitfalls: Some platforms divide by reach or followers rather than views; check the denominator before comparing.

kpis.name: Revenue per 1,000 views
kpis.definition: Revenue earned for every thousand views.

kpis.name: Artists and creators
kpis.definition: Distinct artists, authors, channels or directors.

kpis.name: Likes
kpis.definition: Likes or reactions received in the period.

kpis.name: Subscribers per 1,000 views
kpis.definition: Net subscribers gained for every thousand views.

kpis.name: Production budget
kpis.definition: Production budgets of the films released in the period.
pitfalls: Budgets are studio estimates and usually leave out marketing.

kpis.name: Opening gross
kpis.definition: Opening day or weekend takings of the films released in the period.

kpis.name: Gross per screen
kpis.definition: Gross divided across the screens or theatres the films played on.
kpis.formula: Gross ÷ screens, over films with both

variants.label: Gross ÷ screens
variants.caveat: Screen counts are usually for the home market while the gross may be worldwide.

kpis.name: Domestic share of gross
kpis.definition: Share of the worldwide gross earned in the home market.
kpis.formula: Domestic gross ÷ worldwide gross, over films with both

kpis.name: Films grossing above budget
kpis.definition: Share of films, among those with both figures, whose gross exceeded their production budget.
kpis.formula: Films with gross > budget ÷ films with both

variants.label: Gross above budget ÷ films with both

pitfalls: Grossing more than the budget is not breaking even: exhibitors keep part of the gross and marketing costs come on top.

kpis.name: Genres
kpis.definition: Distinct genres or sections in the catalogue.

kpis.name: Languages
kpis.definition: Distinct languages in the catalogue.

kpis.name: Explicit share
kpis.definition: Share of titles or tracks marked explicit.
kpis.formula: Explicit titles ÷ titles with the flag

kpis.name: Average votes per title
kpis.definition: Average number of user votes or ratings per title.

kpis.name: Comments
kpis.definition: Comments received in the period.

kpis.name: Shares
kpis.definition: Shares or reposts in the period.

charts.title: Watch time over time
charts.reason: Hours watched per period are totals, so columns from a zero baseline compare them honestly.

charts.title: Unique viewers over time
charts.reason: Distinct viewers recounted for each period, never summed across days, read best as a line.

charts.title: Views over time
charts.reason: Views per period are totals: columns from a zero baseline show growth and seasonality.

charts.title: Top titles by watch time
charts.reason: Watch time across many titles: sorted horizontal bars keep the names readable. Top 15 plus Others.

charts.title: Watch time by device
charts.reason: Part-to-whole across a handful of devices (TV, mobile, web): a donut shows the split at a glance.

charts.title: Watch time by genre
charts.reason: Share of listening or viewing time by genre: a treemap shows the big genres and the long tail together.

charts.title: Top artists and creators
charts.reason: Listening or viewing time by artist or creator, sorted so the favourites stand out.

charts.title: Watch time by country
charts.reason: Watch time across many countries: sorted bars of the top 10 plus Others.

charts.title: When people watch
charts.reason: Two time dimensions and one count: a weekday × hour heatmap shows prime time, for scheduling releases and notifications.

charts.title: Completion rate by content type
charts.reason: A rate across a few formats: bars of the recomputed completion rate, with types under 30 plays hidden.

charts.title: Skip rate by artist

charts.title: Watch-time concentration (Pareto)
charts.reason: How hit-driven viewing is: each title's share as columns and the cumulative share as a line on one 0–100% axis.

charts.title: Title performance

charts.title: Views by publish month

charts.title: Net subscribers over time
charts.reason: Gains minus losses per period can go below zero, so columns from a zero baseline show both.

charts.title: Revenue over time
charts.reason: Revenue per period is a total: columns from a zero baseline compare months honestly.

charts.title: Top content by views
charts.reason: Views across many videos or articles: sorted horizontal bars keep titles readable. Top 15 plus Others.

charts.title: Views by author or channel
charts.reason: Views by author, artist or channel, sorted so the biggest contributors stand out.

charts.title: Views by genre or section
charts.reason: Share of views by section or genre: a treemap shows the big sections and the long tail together.

charts.title: Views by format

charts.title: Engagement rate by format
charts.reason: A rate across a few formats: bars of the recomputed engagement rate, formats with under 10 items hidden.

charts.title: Views vs average view duration
charts.reason: Two measures per title: a scatter separates content that is clicked but abandoned from content that holds attention.

charts.title: Revenue per 1,000 views by format
charts.reason: A rate across formats: bars of revenue per thousand views, recomputed for each format.

charts.title: Content performance
charts.reason: Several measures per video or article: a sortable table carries more than any single chart.

charts.title: Titles added over time
charts.reason: Titles counted by when they joined the catalogue: columns show how fast the library grows.

charts.title: Titles by release date
charts.reason: Titles by year of release: columns show how old or new the catalogue is.

charts.title: Titles by genre
charts.reason: Titles across many genres: sorted horizontal bars keep the names readable. Top 15 plus Others.

charts.title: Titles by type
charts.reason: Part-to-whole across a few formats (movies, series): a donut shows the split at a glance.

charts.title: Titles by maturity rating
charts.reason: Titles by audience rating: bars show which age groups the catalogue serves.

charts.title: Titles by country
charts.reason: Where the titles come from: sorted bars of the top 10 countries plus Others.

charts.title: Titles by release year
charts.reason: Release years banded into a histogram show the age profile of the catalogue.

charts.title: Average rating by genre
charts.reason: An average compared across genres: sorted bars, with genres under 10 titles hidden so a few ratings do not rank them.

charts.title: Distribution of runtime
charts.reason: A histogram of runtimes shows the typical length and the outliers that an average hides.

charts.title: Distribution of ratings
charts.reason: Ratings bunch together: a histogram shows how many titles sit in each band.

charts.title: Average popularity by genre
charts.reason: An average compared across genres: sorted bars, small genres hidden.

charts.title: Genre profile
charts.reason: Several measures per genre: a sortable table carries more than any single chart.

charts.title: Artists and creators
charts.reason: Several measures per artist, director or author in one sortable table.

charts.title: Box office gross by release period
charts.reason: The gross of the films released in each period: columns compare release slates honestly.

charts.title: Films released
charts.reason: Films released per period are counts: columns show how crowded each period was.

charts.title: Top films by gross
charts.reason: Gross across many films: sorted horizontal bars keep the titles readable. Top 15 plus Others.

charts.title: Gross by distributor
charts.reason: Market share of distributors or studios: sorted bars of the top 10 plus Others.

charts.title: Gross by genre
charts.reason: Share of box office by genre: a treemap shows the big genres and the rest together.

charts.title: Films by verdict
charts.reason: Part-to-whole across a few verdicts (hit, average, flop): a donut shows the split at a glance.

charts.reason: Two money measures per film: a scatter shows which films earned more, or less, than their budget suggests.

charts.title: Gross-to-budget multiple by genre
charts.reason: A ratio compared across genres, recomputed from summed gross and budget, with genres under five films hidden.

charts.title: Box-office concentration (Pareto)
charts.reason: How hit-driven the slate is: each film's share as columns and the cumulative share as a line on one 0–100% axis.

charts.title: Film performance
charts.reason: Several measures per film: a sortable table carries more than any single chart.

pitfalls: Each platform counts a view, play or stream its own way, so views and completion compare only within one platform.
Unique viewers never add up across titles, days or devices: they are recounted for every period and group.
Lifetime figures per title favour older titles, which have had longer to collect views; compare titles of a similar age.
Box-office figures mix markets and bases: domestic, overseas and worldwide, and nett versus gross collections in India, are different numbers; keep to one.
A catalogue lists what is available, not what was watched: title counts say nothing about demand.
Rates such as completion, skip and engagement are recomputed from counts for every period and group, never averaged across titles.
